review.reviewBody:
People definitely love these cookies! I do a few adjustments to the recipe to make it less sweet and divide out the goodness a little more... I cut the amount of brown sugar to 1 cup and the white sugar to 3/4 cup. I use half quick oats and half old fashioned oats. And so I can get chocolate in tinier bits all over the cookies, I use mini baking M and Ms and the mini chocolate chips. I tried it with chunky PB but found the smooth PB tasted a tad bit better. 

I was fooled the first time and waited until they looked done before I took them out. That meant they weren't as chewy so make sure to take them out right before they look done!

These cookies were very good, but I only gave it 4 stars because there were too many chocolate candies and chocolate chips. Next time I would use 1/2 cup chocolate candies and 1/2 cup chocolate chips. 

Another minor issue is that some of the cookies wouldn't come off the hot pan cleanly. I think baking the cookies on parchment paper on a cookie sheet would solve that issue.

I will definitely make these again. Crisp on the outside and chewy on the inside! I made a couple changes that I'll keep: added 1/2 tsp salt, reduced the brown sugar to 1 cup, reduced the white sugar to 3/4 cup. I reduced the chips and candy-coated milk chocolate pieces to 1/2 cup each so I could add a 1/2 cup raisens and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. The flavors were kind of lost. Next time I'll probably leave out the candies and add the full cup of chocolate chips as the recipe says. I used parchment paper and baked them for 15 min exactly. It yielded about 70 cookies. I'd highly recommend them!

Updated: I've made these several times and still love this recipe as is. The first time I made them, I agreed with some reviews that they are a tad "grainy" as others put it, due to the amount of oats. I liked them that way, but wondered if they'd be better for others if I tried using part flour (1 c.) instead as someone else recommended. I regret trying it. They weren't even nearly as good. I always stick to the amount of oats called for now. I also disagree with those who say they're too sweet. It's a monster cookie and supposed to be pretty sweet and I feel like the peanut butter is the prominent taste in these. The only substitution I would suggest making is using whatever chips/candy combination you like best, still totaling 2 cups combined. I also think the mini baking M&Ms worked better than regular ones. I like them best with 1 cup of those and 1/2 cup each mini semisweet chocolate chips and regular white chocolate chips. I'd also recommend starting you're timer at 10 minutes or less. Mine are perfect at 11 minutes using a cookie scoop (1 tbsp size) slightly heaping to form them. I also gently press them together once they're on the pan to keep loose chocolate pieces in place.
I have been making these for many years in a true MONSTER size: 1/4 cup scoop yields 24, 1/3 cup yields 18. They're a favorite of sports teams, soldiers, and all my kids.

Cut sugar, per reviewers recommendation to 1 c. Brown and 1/2 c. White. Also mistakenly picked up quick cooking oats and used only 4 c. hich turned out well as we use all natural peanut butter which can be runnier than standard Jif or Skippy brands. The quick cooking oats allowed the grain to soak up more of the natural oils and liquid, I think. I also added 1/2 c. Oat flour bc I didn't want cookies falling apart but I wouldn't necessarily do that step again. They turned out fantastic and will be treats for my sons birthday class tomorrow.

I have made these! so good. I decreased brown sugar 1/2 cup and omitted white by 1/4. I did not use chocolate chips. An ice cream scoop was a bit big. I had to cool 2 minutes on baking sheet or they would fall apart. very chewy. Very good cookies. I got about 36 with this recipe.

Added 1/4 tsp salt. Did'nt have ice-cream scoop so fridgerated dough roughly one hour then rolled dough into bigger than normal balls and baked for 8-11 minutes depending on ball size. Very good recipe! Also added wanuts and 3/4 c raisins.

I made only a third of this recipe and it still produced 30 cookies! I threw in an extra handful of M&Ms and doubled the vanilla. I also used three parts oats and one part regular flour. I didn't have any peanut butter on hand so I used half almond butter and half regular salted butter. They turned out deliciously crispy (but not hard), and salty sweet. I'd make these again the next time we need a break from thick chewy cookies.

These are almost too good. I ate 3 of them right away. The only thing I added was 1/2 tsp of salt. They are great as is. Maybe too great. I made them for tomorrow. Hopefully they make it until then....

Update. I have tried making them different ways. I personally prefer them with quick oats. Tonight I tried making them, but was short on oatmeal. I substituted 1/2 cup of flour instead. It was not the same. Not bad, but more like a regular cookie. Not the same texture at all. I have tried and prefer them with replacing 1/3 of the chocolate with butterscotch chips. Also it is easier to top the cookies with M&M's rather than mixing them in. They will also look better. I do make them with 1/4 cup less brown sugar so it's not such an intense sugar high.

I made these using Wow butter (soy nut butter) since I have a peanut allergy in my house. I also followed the suggestion of another reviewer reducing the brown sugar by 1/2c and the white sugar by 1/4c. These tasted ok but I think if I make them again I will use the full amount. Wow butter must not be as sweet as regular creamy PB. I also used a big scoop and put the dough in the fridge between batches which may be unnecessary when using wow butter. When scooping the cookies onto the cookie sheet, I did press them down a bit as they didn't spread as much as in the oven as I anticipated. I rated my version 3 stars; more sugar might improve it.
It's fabulous! I have been asked for the recipe a number of times.
The cookies are very good, but when I took them out of the oven they just wouldn't hold their shape

GREAT HEALTHY COOKIES! NO FLOUR! Big thick filling cookies. Nutritious breakfast cookies. I cut the brown sugar to 1 cup and the white sugar down to 1/2 cup and it was just right. It only made 30 cookies though.
Best monster cookie ever. Love it with butterscotch chips, m&m, choc chip. Yummmm.
I always let these sit on the cookie sheet for a full minute before taking them off.
I make these in my P.C. bar pan! So easy and delicious!

These are just so delicious, and because of the peanut butter and oats, are slightly less junk-y. I like to use walnuts in place of some of the chips and M&M's. Also, beware of over-baking them. They're deliciously chewy in my oven after only about 8 minutes.
